# Uoink v3.12.0
A local library of the YouTube videos, podcasts and articles you study, saved on your Windows PC, that your AI can search and cite with timestamps.
New in 3.12.0: every download ships Whisper's base model (OpenAI Whisper, MIT), so a video without captions is transcribed locally from the first capture with no model download. Other sizes download only when a person asks, and Uoink never downloads a model during a capture. Needs-attention badges now name the problem.

## What it does
- Capture YouTube videos with transcripts, frames, and comments.
- Save X posts and videos, podcasts, articles, and Reddit threads.
- Keep everything on your disk as Markdown + JSON, with a local search index.
- Let your AI search the library and cite timestamps.
- Run five local research playbooks on your saved sources.
- Get writing help in your voice with Voice DNA and Writing Studio.

## Set it up with an agent (Windows 10/11)
Windows 10/11, plus a Mac preview for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later). Uoink v3.12.0 is free and MIT-licensed; the unsigned Windows installer is about 519 MB. No admin rights needed.
[Agent installation steps](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/blob/main/llms-install.md): download, verify SHA-256, install, and connect.
### An agent can run
1. Download [Uoink-Setup-3.12.0.exe](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.12.0/Uoink-Setup-3.12.0.exe) to `$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.12.0.exe`.
2. Before running it, compare `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.12.0.exe"` with the installer entry in [SHA256SUMS.txt](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.12.0/SHA256SUMS.txt).
3. Install per user: `Start-Process -Wait -FilePath "$env:TEMP\Uoink-Setup-3.12.0.exe" -ArgumentList '/VERYSILENT','/SUPPRESSMSGBOXES','/NORESTART'`. It installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink` with Add the uoink command to PATH for AI agents checked by default. Installing over the previous release keeps the library and saved captures; upgrading from before 3.11.0 rebuilds the local keyword search index once.
4. Open a new terminal, run `uoink status`, then connect a client below. Silent install does not start Uoink; MCP works without it running. For the dashboard, browser button, and monitored-playlist polling, start "Uoink" from the Start menu or run `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\python\pythonw.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\server.py"` in PowerShell.
### The person must do
- Allow the unsigned installer if Windows asks. For SmartScreen, choose More info, then Run anyway.
- For the optional browser button: open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select %LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink\extension. An agent can capture without the button.
Chrome (tested); other Chromium browsers such as Edge and Brave may work but are not tested.
Click the puzzle-piece Extensions icon in the toolbar and pin Uoink so the Uoink button stays visible.
- After updating, reload the extension once. If its ID changes to bkcapfidedhfcjpmjabeopfbcjcbmdmi, reapply extension preferences; saved captures are unaffected.

## Set it up on a Mac (preview)
Mac preview: Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later; Intel Macs are not supported. The app and DMG are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS asks only its standard "downloaded from the internet" question.
1. Download [Uoink-3.12.0-macos-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.12.0/Uoink-3.12.0-macos-arm64.dmg) and check it against the SHA-256 on the release page. Open it, drag Uoink to Applications, eject the disk, and open Uoink from Applications.
2. Optional browser button: in Chrome, open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, press ⌘⇧G and paste `~/Library/Application Support/Uoink/extension` (the dashboard's Get the extension card copies it).
3. The uoink command is `/Applications/Uoink.app/Contents/Helpers/uoink`; the app does not change PATH, so link it into a folder on PATH. Run `uoink status`, then `uoink connect <client>` for a recipe with the app's paths. Claude Desktop: open [uoink-3.12.0-macos.mcpb](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.12.0/uoink-3.12.0-macos.mcpb), not the Windows bundle.
Not on the Mac yet: self-update and library mirroring. MCP clients on a Mac are not yet tested.

## Connect your AI
Official MCP registry: io.github.ryanbiddy/uoink
- MCP SDK 2.3.0: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex connect as before; apps that speak the 2026-07-28 MCP protocol can also connect. No action needed.
- Setup recipes: `uoink connect --list` prints setup choices for 48 clients and integrations, 10 of them new in 3.11.0; 45 are checked against each client's official documentation, and each recipe prints its verification status. Run `uoink connect <client>` for config or instructions and their destination; it does not edit client settings. Run the printed Claude Code command in PowerShell; merge other clients' entries into the location shown, then restart their MCP connection. Recipes list a Linux location where the client has a Linux setup.
- Codex: `uoink connect codex` prints tables for `~/.codex/config.toml`. VS Code: `uoink connect vscode` prints config for `.vscode/mcp.json`. The dashboard's Add to Cursor / Add to VS Code buttons open the client's review flow; acceptance of these buttons is not yet tested.
- Uoink skill for Claude Code, Codex, pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw: `uoink skill path` locates it; `uoink skill install --to <dir>` copies it with references into a uoink subfolder of the parent skills directory. Restart the agent or reload its skills.
- Claude Code plugin for a default install: `claude plugin marketplace add ryanbiddy/uoink-agent-kit`, then `claude plugin install uoink@uoink`. Restart Claude Code and enable the plugin MCP server when prompted. Custom installs use `uoink connect claude-code` plus the standalone skill; avoid duplicate MCP entries.
- CLI examples: `uoink search "working memory" --limit 5`, `uoink recent --limit 10`, `uoink note "A useful thought" --title "Research note"`. Agents can search sources, read evidence, capture URLs, save notes, and call registry tools. Local reads work without the helper running; capture and paid tools keep their existing gates. The agent must be able to execute Uoink on the computer holding the library.
3.12.0 Agent Install 30 (installed build, isolated profile): __RECEIPT30__. Earlier, 3.11.1 Agent Install 27: 11/11 PASS, including stdio with 91 full / 35 core / 91 modern tools and Claude Code 2.1.310 (haiku) connected with 91 tools and a get_schema_version call. Codex CLI was not re-tested in receipt 27. Full receipt scope: https://uoink.app/llms-full.txt.

Earlier testing with the installed 3.11.0 build in an isolated profile: Claude Code 2.1.308 over MCP (all 91 tools listed; a tool called) and Codex CLI 0.153.4 over MCP (two tools called). From 3.10.0 testing: Claude Code with the skill and CLI only (skill loaded; uoink note and uoink recent ran). The Claude Code plugin loads its skill and starts its MCP server; its tool calls were not run end to end because the test install is isolated from a normal one. Not yet tested: Gemini CLI and pi (no sign-in on the test machine) and every other uoink connect recipe. Claude Desktop and Cursor retain their earlier MCP testing status.
- Claude Desktop on Windows: download and open [uoink-3.12.0.mcpb](https://github.com/ryanbiddy/uoink/releases/download/v3.12.0/uoink-3.12.0.mcpb) for one-click setup. It installs as an extension and asks for the Uoink folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Uoink). Enter the full path; Desktop does not expand %LOCALAPPDATA%. Reinstall the bundle and restart Desktop after updating.
- Claude Code (verified on Uoink 3.10.0 with 2.1.302): run in PowerShell: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio uoink -e PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 -e PYTHONUTF8=1 -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\python\python.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Uoink\uoink_mcp.py"`.
- Cursor: use the config below and add `"UOINK_MCP_TOOLSET": "core"` to the server env for the previous 35-tool set. Cursor is reported to send only the first 40 tools to its agent; core stays under that cap.
- Other stdio clients: use this config with absolute paths. Full mode is the default. Cline and Continue were not individually smoke-tested. Continue is set up by hand; the dashboard shows it as connected once its entry launches this install.
`{"mcpServers": {"uoink": {"command": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Uoink\\python\\python.exe", "args": ["%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Uoink\\uoink_mcp.py"], "env": {"PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8", "PYTHONUTF8": "1"}}}}`
Replace %LOCALAPPDATA% in both JSON paths with your full app-data directory; restart the client after saving. See the release testing notes above.
- ChatGPT and claude.ai: copy and paste only; Uoink does not connect to the ChatGPT app over MCP.

## Tools
91 tools over stdio and 91 in the HTTP registry. Every tool is on both transports; consent gates are unchanged.
- Capture: video, playlists, podcasts, pages, X, Reddit, notes, and images.
- Search and citations: library search, clips, evidence cards, chapters, and cited range export.
- Search modes: search no longer requires every word. search_library, search_uoinks, and search_clips take optional `match` ("forgiving" by default, "strict" to require every word) and `mode` ("auto" by default, "keyword", "semantic", "hybrid"); find_mentions takes `match`. Auto uses hybrid when semantic search is ready, otherwise keyword; each response says which mode ran. Quote a passage only when passage_verified is true.
- Semantic search is optional and off until a person turns it on in Uoink Settings (Semantic search) and accepts Google's Gemma terms. Uoink then downloads EmbeddingGemma from Hugging Face once (about 330 MB) and runs it on this computer; it works offline after setup, and searches and saved text stay local.
- Research: playbook packets from local sources and optional paid discovery.
- Writing: Voice DNA, drafts, scripts, and writing checks.
- Workspaces: saved projects and context for your agent.
- Library and sources: queue work, subscriptions, and source consent. Librarian applying is off by default; its quality gate has not passed.
[Tool manifest and schemas](https://uoink.app/mcp/manifest.json).

## Privacy in brief
- Local-first: captures and indexes stay on disk; capture requests contact source sites.
- No account or Uoink-hosted corpus.
- Optional AI calls use your own key. Allowed agents can start paid calls even when automatic analysis is off.
- ScrapeCreators discovery is off by default, uses your own key, and defaults to a 25-credit daily cap; paid calls need credit confirmation and consent.
- Discovery run files are purged daily when older than 90 days.
- Anonymous usage counts are off by default. If turned on in Settings, the helper sends one daily report of counts (tool calls, AI apps by a fixed name list, captures by source, searches) with a random install ID; never content, URLs, titles, paths or search text.
- Model dependencies can send telemetry. Model downloads, thumbnails, and release checks can also contact outside services; this website uses Vercel Web Analytics.
Full disclosures: [llms-full.txt](https://uoink.app/llms-full.txt) and [Privacy](https://uoink.app/privacy).
